existingFlow.before: Git -> CI -> OCI -> Argo CD or Flux -> Kubernetes

operations: Store and query exact Kubernetes objects
Compare, test, approve, and promote changes
Record lifecycle routes, releases, and live observations
configHub.problem: A deployable OCI file is useful, but teams still need to share it, change it, review it, promote it, and understand where it is used.
configHub.result: ConfigHub stores the exact objects as Units and keeps their source, variants, diffs, checks, approvals, promotions, and observations together.

delivery.problem: Delivery should not rerender the source package and produce a different result after review.
delivery.result: cub release publish creates an immutable Space release OCI from the reviewed ConfigHub Units. The same reviewed objects can also be packaged as a portable OCI for anonymous or external consumers.
delivery.rule: Each catalog configuration earns a delivery claim only when its own release OCI, controller result, and workload result have a receipt.

accessModel.anonymous: The work uses no ConfigHub account. Public OCI packages remain useful before anyone claims and saves a configuration.
accessModel.composable: The work can sit before OCI, after OCI, or between an input OCI and an output OCI. A user can choose one shape or combine several; ConfigHub is not required until they want saved records and managed operations.
accessModel.serverless: The work does not depend on ConfigHub Server. It can run as a local command, in CI, or eventually as a hosted public service.

anonymousFlows.result: Start with a Helm chart, AICR recipe, installer package, or Kubernetes files; inspect and test the result; then build a deployable OCI package.
Pull an existing public OCI package to inspect its objects, explain its requirements, run checks, or compare it with another version.
Pull an OCI package, check or change its exact objects, and serve the resulting OCI package without taking ownership of it in ConfigHub.

claimBoundary.after: ConfigHub saves the objects and their history so a team can transform, approve, promote, and roll them out. A team can claim at whichever OCI boundary needs managed records; claiming is not a required first step.
claimBoundary.before: Anonymous users can build, inspect, test, pull, and serve public OCI packages.

executionModes.name: Public hosted service

questions.question: What can a new user do first?
questions.standard: Give one short path from a named input to one inspected, deployable result before introducing ConfigHub accounts, fleets, policy, or Apps.

questions.question: Is testing and understanding this configuration easier than using Helm normally?
questions.standard: Show the rendered objects, the recorded inputs, the relevant comparison or parity result, and the command that repeats the check.

questions.question: Can I find the hooks, CRDs, prerequisites, and other chart quirks?
questions.standard: List them beside the package, explain what each one does, name who performs it, and distinguish a proved route from a proposed route.

questions.question: Can I use the rendered-manifest pattern without giving up my Helm chart?
questions.standard: Keep the chart as source, make the literal Kubernetes objects easy to inspect and save, and explain how later edits and upgrades are handled.

questions.question: Can source-to-OCI be automated?
questions.standard: Name the repeatable command or workflow, record the source and output digests, and state which steps still require a person or target-specific input.

questions.question: Can I bring the chart and values my team or AI produced?
questions.standard: Render them without applying, compare them with known configurations, point out risky or unusual changes, and let the user deploy or save the reviewed result.

questions.question: What happens after the first deployment?
questions.standard: Show how the same reviewed result can become a saved base, a development or production variant, a promotion, and an OCI delivered through Argo CD, Flux, or direct apply.

questions.question: What has not been proved?
questions.standard: Keep missing controller paths, upgrades, target checks, and product work visible. Do not turn one passing path into a general claim.

reviewQuestions.rule: Every example and catalog entry must answer these questions in plain English and link to the exact files or receipts that support the answer.
